thread:
maria: idea dump: build a tiny market-based matcher for continuous batching. tenants submit short "bids" with (priority, token-value, latency-budget, affinity). scheduler runs a cheap match pass to pack high-utility batches while honoring per-tenant SLO floors.
kevin: market sounds cool but what's the tick? 5ms/10ms? OS jitter could kill us.
maria: target 10ms tick on the batching core. single-threaded match pass to avoid locking. fallback to current allocator if match loop > threshold.
nate: scoring thought: utility = revenue - lambda * latency_violation. revenue = value_per_token * tokens. lambda depends on tenant tier. keep simple initially.
alice: where do affinity hints come from? prefixes / kvcache warm tags?
carol: yes — annotate requests with affinity: {cold, warm:key-hash}. match should prefer coalescing same-affinity to reduce KV cache misses.
kevin: eviction model? if a higher-utility bid arrives do we evict queued but not-running batches? warm handoff only. never kill in-flight GPU work.
maria: exact constraint: preempt waiting groups only. running groups complete. We need a bounded number of preemptions per-second to avoid thrash.
infra-bot: canary: market-scheduler branch deployed to staging pool at 2025-10-07T09:12:00Z
nate: fairness: add a per-tenant min-allocation floor and a bid-rate cap. adversarial tenants could spam micro-bids. also apply exponential backoff for frequent winners.
alice: perf budget: matching loop should cost < 1ms on p95. otherwise disable. also track match-latency metric.
carol: observability: emit per-batch: matched_utility, chosen_affinities, match_time_ms, displaced_batches, tenant_fairness_score. need dashboards.
kevin: rollout plan: opt-in via config header and per-pool gate. start with internal tenants then beta. add an override header to force FIFO for experiments.
maria: simulation plan: run sim harness with mixes: 60% short-low-token latency-sensitive, 30% long-high-token background, 10% bursty high-value. measure p50/p95/p99 and gpu-occupancy.
nate: sim should include adversarial bidder scenarios to validate fairness floor. I'll add simple game-theory checks.
alice: implementation sketch:
```
// lightweight bid
struct Bid { tenant_id, value_per_token, est_tokens, max_lat_ms, affinity_tag }
// matching loop
every 10ms on batching core:
  gather bids
  group by latency bucket
  greedy-select to fill batch size maximizing (utility + fairness_bonus)
  if match_time > 2ms -> abort match and fallback to safe allocator
  enqueue batches to gpu_queue
```
carol: also consider a small hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping winners (stability term). record last_winner_time per tenant.
kevin: safety toggles: 1) match-loop-time threshold 2) p99 latency guard that auto-rolls back 3) tenants can opt-out.
maria: success criteria: >=5% better occupancy and no >5% increase in p99 for latency-sensitive tenants.
kevin: what about kernel warming? small winning packs could cause suboptimal kernel utilization. maybe require minimum token floor to dispatch as a separate background packing.
nate: agree. include a pack-merge step: if winning selection produces too-small kernel payload, try to merge with low-priority background to hit efficient kernel sizes.
alice: logging: sample match decisions for 1% of batches to inspect why matches happened. useful for debugging SLO regressions.
carol: ops alerting: alert if match-loop fallbacks > 1% of ticks for 5m, or if displaced_batches/sec spikes.
maria: next steps: nate + alice pair to build simulator + prototype; carol to define telemetry; kevin to add canary flags; i'll author a short RFC appendix w/ invariants.
kevin: +1, schedule sync in 2 days. :thumbsup:
